title: Geometric early warning indicator from stochastic separatrix structure in a random two-state ecosystem model
summary: Under-ice blooms in the Arctic can develop rapidly under conditions where conventional early warning signals based on critical slowing down fail due to strong noise or limited observational records. We analyze noise-induced transitions in a temperature phytoplankton stochastic differential equation model exhibiting bistability between background and bloom states. The committor function defines a stochastic separatrix as its 1/2-isocommittor, and the normal width of the associated transition layer yields a geometric indicator via arc-length averaging.
